source.title: Spectral analysis for a class of integral-difference operators: known facts, new results, and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let phi be a nonnegative normalized equilibrium distribution on the real line, and let K_phi be the integral-difference operator on L2(R, dx) given by (K_phi u)(x) = integral from -infinity to infinity of (u(x) phi(s) - u(s) phi(x)) / |x - s| ds. Suppose phi has compact support and is uniformly separated from zero on that support, and let the restricted operator be P_supp(phi) K_phi P_supp(phi). Apart from the reference case phi0 = chi[-1,1], where the corresponding restricted operator K0 commutes with the second-order differential operator L = (x^2 - 1)d^2/dx^2 + 2x d/dx whose eigenfunctions are Legendre polynomials, can one find a differential or pseudodifferential operator that commutes with the restricted operator for some other such compactly supported equilibrium distribution phi?

evidence.quote: The operators under consideration have the form ᏷ϕ : u(x) −→ ∫∞−∞ (u(x)ϕ(s) − u(s)ϕ(x))/|x − s| ds acting in the Hilbert space L2 (R,dx). Here ϕ(x) is the so-called equilibrium distribution function
The most advanced results can be obtained in the case when equilibrium distribution function has compact support and uniformly separated from zero in the whole support.
In the case of compact support, the spectral analysis of the original operator ᏷ϕ is essentially reduced to the analysis of the restricted operator Kϕ = Psuppϕ ᏷ϕ Psuppϕ .
Theorem 3.2 implies that operator K0 commutes with the operator L = (x2 − 1)(d2 /dx2 ) + 2x(d/dx) generating the Legendre polynomials
It would be rather interesting to find such differential or pseudodifferential operator that commutes with Kϕ for some other ϕ.

accepted.question_text: Consider the Gaussian equilibrium distribution case in which the truncated restricted operator K_phi^a acts on functions on [-a,a] by (K_phi^a u)(x) = integral from -a to a of (u(x) phi(s) - u(s) phi(x)) / |x - s| ds, with phi(x) = C exp(-x^2), and is equivalently rescaled to an operator K_a on [-1,1] with phi_a(x) = C_a exp(-a^2 x^2). Suppose the established asymptotic result is that, for every M > 0, the dimension of the spectral subspace E_a[-M,M] H_a tends to infinity as a tends to infinity, so zero is a spectral concentration point for the limit operator. Do the discrete spectra of these truncated operators condense into continuous spectrum as a tends to infinity, and what are the other spectral properties of the limit operator?

evidence.quote: we study a family of operators Kϕa : u(x) −→ ∫a−a (u(x)ϕ(s) − u(s)ϕ(x))/|x − s| ds on the interval [−a,a]
Ka : u(x) −→ ∫1−1 (u(x)ϕa (s) − u(s)ϕa (x))/|x − s| ds on the interval [−1,1], where ϕa (x) := Ca e−a2x2.
For any M > 0, dim Ea [−M,M]Ᏼa −→ ∞ as a −→ ∞.

Other spectral properties of the limit operator are still unknown. In particular, it would be very interesting to clarify if the discrete spectrum of the truncated operators condenses into continuous one when a → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Let phi be a nonnegative integrable equilibrium distribution with infinite support for the integral-difference operator K_phi on L2(R, dx). In this setting phi cannot be uniformly separated from zero on all of R, the compact-support resolvent-comparison method is unavailable, and the constant-equilibrium reference operator K0 is only defined on finite intervals because the corresponding integrals diverge on infinite intervals. Which alternative reference operator should be chosen and developed for spectral analysis of K_phi when phi has infinite support?

evidence.quote: as ϕ(x) is nonnegative and integrable, it cannot simultaneously have an infinite support and be uniformly separated from zero on the whole axis R.
Another difficulty for functions ϕ(x) with infinite support is due to the fact that in this case, we have no relation similar to (3.51).
reference operator with constant equilibrium distribution function like K0 can be defined only for finite intervals, otherwise, the corresponding integrals diverge.
This brings an idea that for ϕ(x) with infinite support, another reference operator should be chosen and investigated. However, no results in this direction are yet known.

trace.notes: Normalized the single input URL https://zbmath.org/2148592 as a zbMATH resolver record. The zbMATH API identified the exact work, title, author, journal pages, DOI 10.1155/S1026022604401022, and EuDML link.

DOI resolution led to a Wiley landing page that returned a Cloudflare challenge locally. Crossref and OpenAlex confirmed the same DOI, title, and publisher OA PDF URL, but local shell fetches for the publisher PDF and other exact-work hosts failed DNS resolution in the restricted CLI environment. A bounded exact-title recovery found readable exact-work mirrors; the CiteseerX PDF URL was selected as the resolved full-text locator, with the full-text mirror used to inspect page text.

Mapped the readable article text: Section 1 defines the integral-difference operators and equilibrium distributions; Section 3 treats compact-support/reference operators; Section 4 treats Gaussian truncations and Theorem 4.1; Section 5 is the explicit discussion and open-problems region.

Extracted three open-problem candidates from Section 5: finding commuting differential or pseudodifferential operators for non-reference compact-support cases; clarifying whether spectra of Gaussian truncations condense into continuous spectrum; and choosing a new reference operator for infinite-support equilibrium distributions.

Expanded the compact-support commuting-operator question with the integral-difference operator definition, the compact-support and uniform-separation assumptions, the restricted operator, and the Legendre/reference-operator context.
Expanded the Gaussian-limit question with the truncated operator, rescaled operator, Gaussian weight, and the stated spectral-concentration result before asking the unresolved condensation question.

Expanded the infinite-support reference-operator problem with the nonnegative integrability condition, the failure of uniform separation, and the reason the constant-equilibrium reference operator is unavailable on infinite intervals.
No near-duplicate candidates were found; the three accepted questions address distinct compact-support, Gaussian-limit, and infinite-support issues.

All accepted items are self-contained, include solved-status metadata, avoid source-pointing language in question_text, and include verbatim evidence with stable section and printed-page locators from the selected full-text source.
